evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Knowledge of data quality, observability, governance, and lineage
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Responsibilities and qualifications are dominated by rigour signals (data quality, observability, governance, lineage, CI/CD, DataOps) with no velocity/speed language present.
evidence.domain_risk: Monitor data performance, availability, and SLAs
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: SLA and reliability language implies operational consequences but there is no explicit financial-reporting or regulatory-compliance language, so moderate.
evidence.data_team_maturity: Support BI, Analytics, Data Science, and ML teams with reliable data products
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Multiple named specialised data sub-teams (BI, Analytics, Data Science, ML) each being served as distinct consumers signals a mature, established data organization.
evidence.jd_authorship: Collaborate with cross-functional teams to deliver business value
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: The bullets are generic dimensional-modeling and pipeline boilerplate that could describe any analytics engineering contract role, typical of a staffing/recruitment agency posting.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Support BI, Analytics, Data Science, and ML teams with reliable data products
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The primary audience named is the data function itself (BI, Analytics, Data Science, ML teams) rather than commercial, product, or finance stakeholders.
evidence.autonomy_level: Build, optimize, and monitor ELT pipelines and data quality processes
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Verbs are build/monitor/support/collaborate rather than define/own/architect, indicating scoped execution work typical of a freelance contract role.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: No mention of AI tools, AI-assisted coding, or AI-consuming infrastructure anywhere in the JD.
evidence.testing_framing: Experience with CI/CD, version control, and DataOps practices
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: CI/CD and DataOps practices appear as required qualifications/skills without an ownership verb framing them as a responsibility the candidate defines.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Monitor data performance, availability, and SLAs
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Moderate: operational reliability (SLAs, availability, data quality) is a stated concern but there is no compliance, regulatory, or stakeholder-trust framing.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Build, optimize, and monitor ELT pipelines and data quality processes
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The dominant verbs (optimize, monitor, maintain) apply to existing pipelines and data models rather than building new infrastructure from scratch.
